Start to finish Well Dweller was absolutely delightful! Whether enjoying the beautifully realized dark fairy tale world or running around smacking baddies with a stick, everything here is polished quality. The tried and true with a couple tricks gameplay never got stale and had a great difficulty throughout. I was never bashing my head in frustration (Silksong…) nor falling asleep traversing around looking for where to head next (which there's also a nifty hint system if you'd like to cut back next point hunting. Really unnecessary but it's there if you want it.)
The bosses look cute and grotesque and were fun to battle. Usually took me 2-3 attempts to beat.
Music is great too!
About 14ish hours for me (a seasoned 'vania enjoyer) to 100% with no hints.
A huge recommendation for all types of gamers. Easily on my GotY26 shortlist! Totally won me over :)

Bright Memory is a gorgeous, fast-paced action sampler that punches way above its single-dev weight class. The juggling mechanics and grappling-hook combat are addictively fun, though the experience is over in the blink of an eye. If you find it on a deep sale, it's a stellar forty-five minutes of pure eye candy and stylish violence.

Side-scrolling hack and slash platform game with goofy ninjas. With normal difficulty the game isn't very long.

Good:  
+ Reasonable loading times  
+ Controls are quick and accurate  

Bad:  
- Not enough gameplay customization options (e.g. katana is the only main weapon)  
- The character warping bug has not been fixed  
- Many bosses have MASSIVE amount of health  

Ugly:  
* Some sprites are bit hard to identify (e.g. the elevator in tower and some pre-slain corpses)
